endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Foundational: Organizations should have a named monitoring owner(s), a defined review cadence (e.g., quarterly), and documented triggers that warrant re-review or escalation. Even organizations without formal dashboards should have these elements.

evidence.title: Automated stereotactic radiosurgery planning using a human-in-the-loop reasoning large language model agent
evidence.outcome: Presence of deliberative behaviors in agent reasoning traces, reasoning versus non-reasoning model
evidence.effect: Reasoning agent showed prospective constraint verification (457 instances) and trade-off deliberation (609 instances) versus 0 and 7 instances for the standard model; traces serve as auditable logs.
evidence.quote: When prompted to improve conformity, the reasoning model demonstrated systematic planning behaviors including prospective constraint verification (457 instances) and trade-off deliberation (609 instances), while the standard model exhibited none of these deliberative processes (0 and 7 instances, respectively).

commentary.bottom_line: One offline study of 41 retrospective brain metastases radiosurgery cases found that a reasoning agent's traces recorded 457 instances of prospective constraint verification and 609 of trade-off deliberation, against 0 and 7 for a standard model. No study tested whether evaluating trace transparency helps users understand or audit agent actions in practice.

perspectives.view: The only test is a single level 4 simulated study of 41 cases. It counted deliberative behaviors in traces rather than measuring whether reviewers could understand or audit them. Indirectness, single-study imprecision, and a retrospective offline design lower certainty to very low.

Traces that record constraint checks may give reviewers a record for finding planning errors after the fact. The study did not measure whether anyone caught an error using the traces, so it is unknown whether trace review stops harm before treatment is delivered.

More than 1,000 logged deliberation events across 41 cases suggests that traces may be long. The study did not report how much reviewer time trace evaluation required, how faithful traces were to the actual computation, or how review fit into clinical workflow.

The CHAI playbook asks organizations to name a monitoring owner, set a review cadence such as quarterly, and document escalation triggers. That guidance could give trace evaluation a home in governance. No study estimated the staffing or cost of reviewing traces at scale.

The single endorsement comes from a voluntary framework and addresses monitoring structure in general rather than reasoning traces specifically. The supplied sources do not tie trace evaluation to any binding requirement.

commentary.research_gap: Prospective studies should test whether structured evaluation of agent reasoning traces improves clinicians' ability to detect and correct agent errors. They should report trace fidelity, reviewer time, and patient-level outcomes in live workflows.
commentary.underserved_note: The single test did not report patient demographics, payer mix, language, or literacy. It therefore gives no information on whether trace evaluation works for Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations, or for the staff who serve them.
